The MoHRE Emiratization Compliance Agent — built and run on Wakeel.

One officer, one description in plain language, and a governed Microsoft 365 agent that chases business compliance every day — while people keep every decision. Here is the whole story, step by step.

The problem MoHRE described

Emiratization outreach is real work, done by hand.

Officers track hundreds of businesses in a spreadsheet, email each one for its compliance report, wait for replies, check the answers against policy, chase the late ones, and escalate the hard cases. It is slow, repetitive, and easy to let slip — but every judgement still has to be a person's.

The registry
Excel on SharePointBusiness name, contact, sector, compliance status, dates, assigned officer, notes, next action.
The outreach
Microsoft OutlookReport requests, reminders, escalations and the daily officer summary.
The rulebook
SharePointSOPs, Emiratization policies, report templates and approved email templates.
The request — exactly as the officer typed it

No forms. No code. Just describe the job.

This is the real prompt pasted into Wakeel. Everything that follows was generated from it.

wakeel · new agent
Create a Microsoft 365-based G2B Emiratization Compliance Agent for MoHRE.

Use these integrations only:
 • Microsoft Outlook — send outreach emails, receive business responses, send reminders, escalate cases.
 • SharePoint — access SOPs, Emiratization policies, report templates, approved email templates.
 • Excel on SharePoint — maintain the business registry and compliance tracking sheet.

The agent should read the Excel registry to identify businesses requiring outreach, send approved
report-request emails through Outlook, monitor replies, evaluate submitted responses against SharePoint
SOPs and policy documents, update the Excel status, and send follow-ups for missing, incomplete, or
overdue responses.

Track: Business Name, Contact Email, Sector, Compliance Status, Last Outreach Date, Last Response Date,
Assigned Officer, Notes, Next Action.

Support both scheduled daily checks and manual officer-triggered runs.

Statuses: Pending Outreach, Report Requested, Response Received, Incomplete Submission, Under Review,
Follow-up Sent, Escalation Required, Completed.

The agent must not make final legal or enforcement decisions. It reviews responses, identifies
gaps, recommends next actions, updates tracking records, and escalates to MoHRE officers when needed.

Use a professional MoHRE-style tone in all business communications.
PART 1
Building the agent — about five minutes

From a paragraph to a governed, running agent.

Wakeel proposes a full design first, the officer reviews it, and only then is anything built. Nothing is a black box.

1

The officer signs in

Any MoHRE employee signs in with their entity account — no developer, no setup. Wakeel opens in Arabic or English.

wakeel · sign in
2

They describe the agent in chat

Instead of a builder, the officer just writes what they need — the MoHRE prompt above. Wakeel works in the language they use.

wakeel · home
3

Wakeel proposes the architecture — and asks before building

Wakeel reasons through triggers, integrations, registry fields, statuses and guardrails, then shows the whole design: a per-business loop with outreach, review, follow-up and escalation branches, a 16-node flow, the Excel schema and the allowed statuses. It ends with a question — “Shall I go ahead and build this agent?” — with Build and Request changes. You can refine it in plain language before a single thing is created.

wakeel · design proposal
The proposal is fully editable by chatting — e.g. “add an Arabic translation step” or “require officer sign-off before any rejection”.
4

The officer reviews the built flow

On approval Wakeel builds the agent and opens its workspace. Every node is visible and runnable — registry read, per-business loop, outreach, reply monitoring, review against SOPs, Excel update, follow-up, escalation and the daily summary.

wakeel · agent · flow
5

Governance & guardrails are generated automatically

Because it is a government agent, Wakeel writes a policy layer for it: a decision boundary, guardrails, the human-in-the-loop checkpoints, the allowed statuses and the escalation policy. This is what keeps the agent advisory — it recommends, people decide.

wakeel · agent · governance
6

Microsoft 365 is connected — as one product

The officer connects Outlook, SharePoint and Excel. Wakeel’s built-in automation engine handles the Microsoft connectors and the schedule; the agent does the thinking. It’s one Microsoft sign-in, then it runs on your timer — and it can be self-hosted on Azure UAE North for data residency.

triggers · connect M365
integrations
Left: the guided Microsoft 365 connection. Right: the connector catalogue — Outlook, SharePoint and Excel install natively.
7

Test, fine-tune, publish

The officer runs a manual test on a few sample registry rows, adjusts wording, escalation rules or status mapping if needed, and publishes. The agent is now operational — running daily checks and available for manual, officer-triggered runs.

PART 2
The agent at work — every day

One run of the daily compliance cycle.

Scheduled each weekday morning, or launched on demand by an officer. Here is what it does, in order.

📖
STEP 1

Read the registry

Opens the Excel registry on SharePoint and finds businesses needing action.

✉️
STEP 2

Send outreach

Emails approved report-requests through Outlook in a professional MoHRE tone.

👀
STEP 3

Monitor replies

Watches Outlook for business responses and marks them received.

⚖️
STEP 4

Review vs SOPs

Compares each submission to SharePoint policies; flags missing or unclear items.

✏️
STEP 5

Update Excel

Writes status, dates, notes, assigned officer and the next action.

🔔
STEP 6

Follow up

Sends a polite reminder for missing, incomplete or overdue responses.

🚩
STEP 7

Escalate

Marks hard cases “Escalation Required” and notifies the assigned officer.

📊
STEP 8

Daily summary

Emails officers a recap: outreach sent, replies, incomplete cases, escalations, completed.

The officer decides — always

The agent drafts; the officer approves, edits or rejects before anything leaves MoHRE. Escalations and final outcomes wait in the officer’s inbox.

wakeel · inbox

Everything is measured

Runs, success rate, approvals and per-agent performance — a live view of how the compliance effort is going across the register.

wakeel · analytics

When the officer confirms a case is resolved, its status becomes Completed — and the agent moves on to the next business.

The line that never moves

What the agent does — and what it will never do.

✓ The agent handles the legwork

  • Reads the registry and identifies who needs action
  • Drafts and sends approved outreach, reminders and escalations
  • Reviews responses against SOPs and identifies gaps
  • Keeps the Excel registry accurate and up to date
  • Recommends the next action and a daily summary

✕ People keep every judgement

  • No final legal or enforcement decisions
  • No penalties, exemptions or regulatory rulings
  • Nothing marked Completed without officer confirmation
  • No emails to anyone outside the registry without approval
  • No data leaves the MoHRE Microsoft 365 tenant
